The throat warns of the breath.

bestiary.codenamecoraline.title: Bestiary
bestiary.codenamecoraline.intro: A traveller's notes on the creatures folklore left in the ruins: the mystic side, how they attack and where to find them. Every new creature gets a chapter.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.redcap.name: Redcap
bestiary.codenamecoraline.redcap.cover.c: Fig. 1: a spear Redcap, in profile.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.redcap.folklor: Also called Powrie or Dunter, the Redcap belongs to the Unseelie Court: the sinister caste of the fairy folk of the Scottish borders. It plays no pranks: it kills whoever crosses its path, unprovoked. They say it is born where there was massacre and tyranny, and that every bloody ruin breeds its own.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.redcap.blood.b: The cap is the heart of the creature. The tales swear its cloth must be dyed with fresh blood, or the goblin withers. So it never flees a fight and never leaves a traveller in peace. And it wears iron boots, the metal that harms the fair folk: a blasphemy that makes it even more feared.
They strike from very close, in quick successive cuts. No reach: beyond a block and a half you are safe.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.redcap.claws.b: Unarmed, they scratch up close. From afar they hurl pebbles: between 5 and 16 blocks. They anticipate your step.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.redcap.attacks: SPEAR: a long, slow thrust of about two blocks. Sidestep it and get inside its reach. DAGGER: quick cuts up close; back off between blows. CLAWS: scratch up close and aim the pebble where you will be: change direction, never run in a straight line.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.redcap.pack.bo: When one picks a victim it laughs, and the others take the same target. Spear and dagger Redcaps surround, take opposite sides and charge together. The claws stay behind, lobbing pebbles. Hurting one wakes them all. Fight in a corridor, back to the wall.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.redcap.cap.bod: Whoever wears the cap is taken for one of their own: they do not attack and they help against whoever hurts the wearer. Take it off in their sight and the pack's fury lasts half a minute.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.redcap.where.b: Ruins of old blood: strongholds, ruined portals, trail ruins, ancient cities and abandoned pillager towers, preferably at night, and almost always one to a place. (Traveller's note: I never saw one born on its own; for now it is only summoned with the egg.)
bestiary.codenamecoraline.redcap.drops.b: Nail and tooth: common, useful to those who know potions. Rusted weapons: rare, worn at random, from nearly new to nearly broken; only the one that carried a weapon drops it. The cap: very rare, and the most valuable of all. Only taken from one you kill with your own hands.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.basilisk.name: Basilisk
bestiary.codenamecoraline.basilisk.anato: A low, fin-tailed amphibian bearing two huge golden growths. These false eyes never blink. Its real eyes are tiny points beside the snout. Its throat swells before it exhales. Inspired by the Basilisks of Elden Ring.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.basilisk.habit: Hostile and common. Groups of four to eight appear in swamps and mangroves, even during the day. They also inhabit caves throughout the Overworld: beneath the terrain, with no visible sky and light seven or lower. They need solid ground and never spawn in Peaceful. They leap at travellers within ten blocks.
Listen for the inhale: you have 1.2 seconds to move. The mist lasts five seconds within 3.5 blocks of its centre. It applies Blindness and Wither III for five seconds: hearts turn black and health drains rapidly. Solid walls block exposure.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.basilisk.survi: Leave the mist. Wither III can kill; milk removes both effects. The potion brewed from a Basilisk leg, eye and tail protects against both for three minutes. Fire deals 50% extra damage; swords deal 25% extra. Poison, Wither and Darkness cannot harm the creature.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.basilisk.light: Hold a soul torch or soul lantern in either hand. The Basilisk stops attacking and retreats about six blocks. Strike it yourself and it remembers you: your soul flame will no longer repel that individual. Existing mist remains dangerous.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.basilisk.spoil: On death, a Basilisk may drop one leg (50%), one eye (25%) and one tail (35%). Rolls are independent, in any biome. All three parts are used, in that order, at a brewing stand to prepare Wither and Blindness Resistance.
Fuel the stand with blaze powder. Brew water with nether wart, then leg, eye and tail in order. Each step takes twenty seconds for up to three bottles. Cures and blocks Wither and Blindness for three minutes; redstone extends to eight. Gunpowder: splash. Dragon breath: lingering. Milk removes protection.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.lithophage.ana: The Lithophage (Litófago) is an ancient subterranean creature formed of hardened clay and minerals. It remains motionless for long periods and awakens when it detects a threat in its territory.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.lithophage.hab: Inhabits Lush Caves primarily and Dripstone Caves secondarily, between Y = -20 and Y = 20. Spawns in dark chambers in groups of 1 to 2 (rarely 3). Initially dormant, it awakens within 12 blocks and pursues up to 20 blocks before returning to rest.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.lithophage.att: Danger level: high in narrow tunnels. Bears 36 HP (18 hearts), 6 mineral armor, heavy 0.22 movement speed and moderate knockback resistance (55%). Combines heavy melee strikes with ranged shard fire.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.lithophage.com: Slag Slam: vertical strike dealing 5 HP after a 0.6 s wind-up. Tectonic Sweep: lateral frontal-arc swing dealing 4 HP after 0.8 s.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.lithophage.tac: Amber Shard: channels mineral energy and fires a 4 HP projectile every 3 to 5 seconds, blocked by solid walls. After each heavy attack, the Lithophage enters recovery (0.6 to 0.9 s), opening a clear window to counter-attack.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.lithophage.spo: I: ancient clay. II: amber core.
Upon collapsing, it yields 12 experience, Ancient Clay Fragment (1 to 2, common) and, with a lower chance, a Mineral Amber Core.
item.codenamecoraline.last_gift_collecto: Nicolas Noel, the Renegade Spawn Egg
entity.codenamecoraline.last_gift_collec: The Collector of the Last Gift
The Silent Bell echoes across the frozen sky...
The Silent Bell must be rung upon Packed Ice.
The winter gale does not answer here. Seek a Snowy Taiga or Grove.
Nicolas Noel only crosses the sky at night.
The sky and clearing around the ice must be unobstructed.
Nicolas Noel already walks these snows.
advancements.codenamecoraline.bosses.the: Nicolas Noel once brought the gifts. The villages stopped paying, and he came back as the Collector of the Last Gift. Defeat the Renegade and close the last debt of the solstice.
subtitles.codenamecoraline.entity.last_g: Nicolas Noel's sleigh cuts the sky
bestiary.codenamecoraline.last_gift_coll: Santa hat, long nose, great beard and greataxe.

A colossal 4.5-block fey in a burgundy coat trimmed with pale fur. A blue-grey face with a long, cold nose glares from under a Santa hat and a beard that reaches his belt. He carries a greataxe and a sack stitched with a skull.

Nicolas Noel once carried the gifts of the solstice, and every gift was a pledge. The villages stopped paying and he came back as the Collector of the Last Gift, with the same axe that cut his promise. Craft the Silent Bell (bell, 4 packed ice, soul lantern) and ring it at night on packed ice in a Snowy Taiga or Grove under open sky. The advancements tell the rest of his story.

420 HP, 10 armor (+4 toughness), 90% knockback resistance; he never freezes and powder snow does not hold him. Stages begin at 80, 60, 40, 20 and 10% health: 2 Gaze, Whirlwind and crescents; 3 comets, gift rain and Gift Mimics; 4 Frost Cone; 5 Frenzy (+4 damage); 6 RAGE: speed, armor and damage amplified.

His rhythm is never the same: wind-ups stretch and shrink, attacks chain into combos and he leads his shots. He answers kiting with comets and gift rain, and a pillar with magic. Look away from his Gaze, leave the gold-and-red rings before the presents land, and kill the Gift Mimics before they burst.
Overhead axe chop and a trailing comet.

Axe: cleave 11, overhead chop waves 7, whirlwind 6, crescent wave 9. Stomp 9, Solstice Leap 12. Magic: comets 8 (homing), gift rain 10, Frost Cone 8 with freezing, Gaze 5. Gift Mimics bite for 5 and burst for 7. Frenzy adds 4 to every hit; Rage multiplies by 1.5.
I: Greataxe. II: Cracked Bell. III: Thread. IV: Seal.

On his final collapse: 100 XP and the advancement The Final Delivery. A Christmas gift falls and pops open on a chest holding the Renegade's Greataxe (always), 1 Cracked Bell, 2 to 4 Frostbound Threads and a 20% chance for the rare Solstice Seal. His Gift Mimics vanish with him.
advancements.codenamecoraline.bosses.sil: The Bell That Does Not Ring
They say the last gift of winter came with a bell that never sounds. Craft the Silent Bell: a bell, packed ice and a soul lantern.
advancements.codenamecoraline.bosses.the: Every gift at the solstice was a pledge, and every pledge falls due. Ring the bell on packed ice, at night, in the snow, and Nicolas Noel will answer.
The Day the Sleigh Fell Silent
Nicolas's sleigh bell cracked the day the last village went quiet. Take the Cracked Bell from his gift.
Nicolas Noel cut his own promise with this axe, and called his gifts to heel with it. Now it is yours to carry.
Back when giving was an honour and not a debt, Nicolas sealed the first gift with this. Very few ever find it.
Nicolas Noel's axe. Right-click: call 3 Gift Mimics to fight for you.
Each call wears the axe (250 durability).
The axe is too worn to call more gifts.
Your Gift Mimics are still around.
subtitles.codenamecoraline.entity.canopy: The Canopy Breaker bellows in pain
Heavy footsteps of the Canopy Breaker
The Canopy Breaker flies into a fury
entity.codenamecoraline.canopy_breaker.s: The branches tremble. Something heavy is coming down from the canopy...
The idol must be set against a tree trunk.
Only the oldest forests answer: an old-growth taiga or a dark forest.
The beast only comes down at night.
There are too few old trees around to carry him.
There is no clearing near the trunk for him to land in.
The Canopy Breaker already rules this forest.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.canopy_breaker: Long arms, a bowed back and the Deadroot Club.

An ape-like beast of 3.1 blocks, with mossy bark-grey fur, arms longer than its legs and knuckles worn into hooks. On the move it runs on four limbs; to fight it draws a club of dead root from its back and stands. Its eyes glow amber in the dark of the canopy.

Loggers who cut the oldest trees said something up in the crown cut back. They carved hollow idols from dark oak, bone and moss to ask it to come down. Use the Hollow Trunk Idol on a log in an old-growth taiga or a dark forest, at night, with many trees around and a clearing nearby. A failed use never spends the idol and tells you what is missing.

200 HP, 8 armor, speed 0.33 on the ground, 3.1 blocks tall. Stage 1 guards the forest floor. At 60% health he becomes the Canopy Hunter and takes to the trees: climbing trunks, crossing between canopies in real jumps and dropping on you. At 25% he becomes the Fury of the Timber: faster, with shorter pauses. Each change happens once.

He never swings at empty air: watch the club. A shield will not save you: every blow of the club breaks the guard, and his free hand seizes whoever stays close, lifts them overhead and hurls them across the clearing. When he rears up with both fists, get away: the pound throws everyone around him into the air. He bounds across open ground and springs up at anyone on a pillar, so height is no refuge. When he climbs, he is committed: break the trunk he is on, or leave the mark of the Canopy Drop.
Overhead slam and the mark on the ground.

Trunk Slam 7, Canopy Sweep 5, Brute Lunge 6, Backhand 4, Canopy Drop 8, Fist Pound 9 (throws you up), Grab and Throw 3 and 8 (a hand no shield can stop). Every blow has a visible wind-up and a recovery window in which he can be staggered by a heavy hit; a missed grab leaves him open.
I: Club. II: Resin. III: Heartwood.

On defeat, once: 60 XP, 2 to 4 Canopy Resin, 50% for a Heartwood Splinter and 30% for the Deadroot Club. The advancements Hollow Trunk, Something Answers, Felled Beast and Dead Root keep the rest of the story.
advancements.codenamecoraline.bosses.can: Loggers carved idols out of dark oak, bone and moss to call down what lives in the crowns. Craft a Hollow Trunk Idol.
Set the idol against a log in an old-growth taiga or a dark forest, at night, with many trees around. The canopy will answer.
Defeat the Canopy Breaker, whether on the forest floor, in the branches or in the air between the trees.
The beast carried a club of dead root on its back for longer than the forest has been standing. Take the Deadroot Club.
item.codenamecoraline.deadroot_club.lore: Hold right-click on the ground, release: the club pulls you where you look. Hold Shift in the air to dive and slam.
Shift + right-click calls Bark Macaques to fight beside you.
item.codenamecoraline.deadroot_club.airb: You must be on the ground to leap.
item.codenamecoraline.deadroot_club.too_: The club is too worn to call anyone.
item.codenamecoraline.deadroot_club.summ: Enough Bark Macaques already fight for you.
item.codenamecoraline.crimson_oath_great: Right-click: Crimson Dash, a 6-block advance that cuts everything in its line.
The blade an oathbound general never lowered.
entity.codenamecoraline.crimson_commande: The deepslate trembles. Iron footsteps echo through the hall...
The crest must be set on deepslate bricks or polished deepslate.
The hall is too cramped: he needs 5x5x5 free blocks above the deepslate.
A Crimson Commander already guards this hall (less than 48 blocks away).
advancements.codenamecoraline.bosses.com: Summon the Crimson Commander on deepslate bricks.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.crimson_comman: Before the deepslate swallowed the kingdom, a general swore to guard the throne hall until his king returned. The king never did. Centuries of intruders have dyed his plate a deep crimson and torn his royal cape to rags, but the oath still stands: he walks the dark chambers below layer zero in silence and fights with the discipline of one who has never lost a duel. Whoever sets the Stained Oath Crest on deepslate bricks or polished deepslate, with a free hall of 5x5x5 blocks above it, is granted an audience.
3.5 blocks of plate, a T-visored helm and the sword on his shoulder.

A knight 3.5 blocks tall (a box 1.1 blocks wide) in crimson plate over iron-grey mail. Wide spiked pauldrons, a closed helm whose T visor leaks a ruby glow, horns and a crest, and a red plume falling down his back. 220 HP, 14 armor and 6 armor toughness, speed 0.29, 12 base damage, 75% knockback resistance. Immune to fire, lava, freezing and drowning, walks on powder snow, takes only 20% of fall damage and never burns in daylight.
The Dash Thrust: body leaning in, blade level with the target.

Crimson Slash: 12 damage in a 140 degree sweep in front of him, reach 3.8. Dash Thrust: up to 9 blocks to where you will be, 15 damage and Slowness I. Heavy Overhead Slam: both hands on the grip, a 2-block leap and the blade driven into the ground, 20 damage within 2 blocks and 12 up to 4, throws you up and disables shields for 5 s. Blood Crescent Wave: a crescent that flies 22 blocks for 13 damage; solid blocks stop it.

He punishes haste. After three blows within two seconds, or when all his attacks are cooling down, he plants his legs and crosses the sword before his chest: the guard stops 75% of frontal damage, turns arrows back and answers any frontal melee blow with a 14-damage Riposte that throws you far. Do not strike his front while the sword is crossed: circle behind him or use the pause to heal. Against the Heavy Overhead Slam, leave the gold and crimson ring drawn on the floor and punish the 26 ticks he spends pulling the blade free. Against the Dash, sidestep in the last moments of the wind-up. He never swings at the air: step out of reach during a wind-up and he calls it off. Fleeing or climbing a pillar will not save you: he leaps at you or sends the wave.

Iron Vigil (100% to 60%): Slash, Dash and Guard; the wave and the overhead slam only against those who flee or hide up high. Awakened Oath (below 60%, once): he raises the sword in a crimson pulse, calls two Crimson Ash Vanguards, grows faster (0.32) and every cooldown drops by 20%; the slam and the wave join the rotation. Fury of the Last Commander (below 25%, once): visor and blade burn, speed 0.35, 25% more damage, and the Dash can chain straight into the Heavy Overhead Slam. The Vanguards (28 HP, 6 damage) last 30 seconds, never strike their master, leave no spoils and turn to ash when he falls.
I: Greatsword. II: Plate Shard. III: Crest.

On defeat, once: 250 XP, 3 to 6 Crimson Plate Shards, a 25% chance of a Stained Oath Crest and, at the end of his last kneel, the Crimson Oath Greatsword planted where he fell. The sword can also be forged from 4 Shards, 1 Crest and 1 netherite sword. Its right-click performs the Crimson Dash: a 6-block advance, 8 damage in line, 8 durability and a 6-second cooldown.
bossbar.codenamecoraline.ten_threads_wit: Esther, the Witch of Ten Threads
item.codenamecoraline.ten_threads_witch_: Witch of Ten Threads Spawn Egg
Shift + right-click: change the stance of the threads.
Hunting, Control and Ruin: ten threads, three ways to pull them.
Stance I: Hunting Threads (haul yourself across)
Stance II: Control Threads (toll and root)
The thread finds nothing to hold on to.
entity.codenamecoraline.ten_threads_witc: The threads tremble in the canopy. Someone is counting you...
The spindle needs a solid block to stand on.
Only the oldest woods answer: dark forest, pale garden, old-growth taiga (or any dense forest at night).
The thread has no room to spin: 5x5x5 free blocks are needed above.
A Matriarch already weaves within 64 blocks.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.ten_threads_wi: The Witch of Ten Threads
Esther, the Seamstress

An old weaver and healer exiled to the oldest woods, Esther refused her own death. She split her fears, pains and memories into ten monstrous vessels of cloth, porcelain, bronze and root. Her true body shrank to a frail old woman barely 1.15 blocks tall, but her mind spread through ten threads of silver ether tied to her Staff of the Living Loom.
The Cocoon of Threads
A frail old woman, a blindfold of lace and a wheel of ten spools.

While any puppet is awake or hanging, the Matriarch cannot be hurt. Each spool on her staff wheel is one puppet: when it falls, its spool bursts. 150 HP, only reachable after the tenth puppet falls. Immune to falls and freezing, she walks on powder snow.
The Crimson Thread
The Cradle Giant winds up: the crimson thread tightens to the staff.

Before each special attack the thread tying the puppet to the staff turns crimson and hums. Cut it with a blow or an arrow and the attack stops, the puppet takes 15% of its health and falls TANGLED for 3.5 s, taking 1.75x damage. Dodging the special attack at the right moment can tangle it too. Use the forest: a trunk in front of the Hound or the Stag stops the charge.
Puppets I to III

I. Sewing Arachnid (80 HP): if you sidestep the Canopy Plunge without jumping, it stakes the ground and is left tangled. II. Porcelain Hound (95 HP): its lunge cracks the porcelain (armour 10 to 0) against a shield or a tree. III. Hollow Bell (110 HP): arrows from above bounce off, only the clapper below takes damage (2x); cut the thread while the Resonance winds up.
Puppets IV to VI

IV. Patchwork Stag (125 HP): stand before a trunk and sidestep its stampede. V. Stitched Rook (115 HP): cut the thread in its dive, or shoot it while it hovers. VI. Hollow Bride (135 HP): after three blows she sidesteps; cut the thread of her Veil as it tightens.
Puppets VII to IX

VII. Skirted Centipede (145 HP): its thread shows when it surfaces again; cut it then. VIII. Root Mother (160 HP, no knockback): circle behind her while she roots and cut the thread. IX. Patchwork Executioner (185 HP): sidestep the Guillotine and strike the seam of its neck (2.5x) from above or along the stuck arm.
Puppet X and the True Face

X. Cradle Giant (220 HP): cut the thread after the sixth needle and it kneels; the Cradle takes 2.5x. When it falls, Esther tears off her blindfold and fights with 150 HP, speed 0.40 and three attacks of her own: the Needle Thrust, the Echo of the Ten Threads and the Storm of the Loom.
Spoils and the Staff
I: Staff. II: Remnant. III: Thimble.

Each puppet leaves a Remnant and two Orbs of Vital Spool (4 HP, 3 hunger, 15 durability repaired). Esther leaves a Seamstress Casket with the Staff of the Ten Threads and 1 to 2 Matriarch's Thimbles. The staff has three stances (Shift + right-click): Hunting (haul yourself 22 blocks), Control (toll and roots, 8 blocks) and Ruin (crushing arms, 22 damage).
advancements.codenamecoraline.bosses.sum: Awaken the Witch of Ten Threads.
advancements.codenamecoraline.bosses.sev: Cut a taut crimson thread while a puppet winds up its attack.
advancements.codenamecoraline.bosses.def: Defeat all ten puppets and the Matriarch.
advancements.codenamecoraline.bosses.obt: Obtain the Staff of the Ten Threads.
subtitles.codenamecoraline.entity.ten_th: A puppet tangles in its threads
subtitles.codenamecoraline.entity.cradle: A cradle creaks and needles fly
dialogue.codenamecoraline.ten_threads_wi: What noisy steps in my forest... Did you come to tear the cloth, or to serve as thread?
Go, my little one... measure the coffin with your needles.
Careful not to break the china... it bites deep when it cracks!
Listen... for whom might my bell be tolling today?
The whole forest bows when the old antlers run!
Look up, wingless little bird... the sky has seams too.
So pretty at the altar... but no one wanted to hold all her hands.
Under the earth, under the skirt... how many fingers fit around your neck?
The earth is hungry, child... let Mother hold your bones!
Nine threads! Let us see if your spine can bear the weight of my verdict!
My last thread... my firstborn! Sleep, sleep while he tears you apart!
Ouch! Do not touch my lines, insolent worm!
My children... you broke every one of them! Then I will be the needle and the shroud myself!
At last... the fingers... may rest...
subtitles.codenamecoraline.entity.fey_ra: Fey Raven resonates with mystic warning
bestiary.codenamecoraline.fey_raven.name: Fey Raven
bestiary.codenamecoraline.fey_raven.anat: Obsidian plumage, silver runes and the vertical third eye.

The Fey Raven (Corvo Feérico) is a twilight messenger of the ancient courts. Above its hooked beak sits a third vertical eye of glowing cyan light, and silver-white runes shimmer along its wing coverts and throat ruff.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.fey_raven.habi: Inhabits Dark Forests primarily, as well as Old Growth Pine Taigas and Cherry Groves above Y = 64. Spawns in small flocks of 1 to 2 perched on high branches and leaves, hunting silverfish and gathering luminous berries.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.fey_raven.tami: Offering Glow Berries to a wild Fey Raven has a 33% chance per berry to earn its loyalty. Once tamed, Glow Berries and Sweet Berries restore 4 HP. Right-clicking with an empty hand cycles between Follow, Sit and Sentinel orbit; jumping close allows it to perch on your left shoulder.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.fey_raven.comb: Diving strike and evasive wing rebound.
With 14 HP and nimble 0.40 flight speed, the Fey Raven harries anyone who strikes its owner with 2 HP diving pecks before rebounding out of reach. It never harms its owner or allied companions.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.fey_raven.sent: Its third eye pierces deception: every 30 seconds, if an invisible or ambushing enemy approaches within 16 blocks, the raven caws a crystalline warning and outlines the threat with Glowing for 5 seconds. Sneak-right-clicking stores a single scroll, book or gem in its leg case.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.fey_raven.spoi: I: Fey Feather. II: Messenger Scroll & Glow Berries.
Yields 1 to 2 common feathers and a 10% chance of a luminescent Fey Feather. Any item entrusted to its messenger scroll case is returned intact.
advancements.codenamecoraline.bosses.fin: Gather Glow Berries to draw the attention of a three-eyed Fey Raven in the high canopies.
advancements.codenamecoraline.bosses.tam: Tame a Fey Raven with Glow Berries and gain a mystic sentinel against unseen threats.
advancements.codenamecoraline.bosses.fey: Obtain a luminescent Fey Feather from the twilight messengers.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.brimstone_sala: Basalt scales, dorsal scutes, and an incandescent sulfur bellows throat.

The Brimstone Salamander is a predatory, magma-dwelling amphibian of ancient fey alchemical lore. Its hide is composed of interlocking volcanic basalt scutes and glowing sulfur blotches, with a luminous bellows throat capable of igniting compressed minerals.

Native to Basalt Deltas, Nether Wastes, and Crimson Forest lava shores between Y = 24 and Y = 48. They bask on warm rocks and swim effortlessly through molten lava. If transported beyond the Nether, they actively seek hot blocks and fires to preserve their inner heat.

Possessing 44 HP, 8 natural armor, and 65% knockback resistance, it is completely immune to lava, fire, and heat. However, water petrifies its scales, and mystical cold shatters its core, causing it to take double damage from freezing.
Combines a sudden 7.0 friction bite, a 160° tail sweep, and a ballistic sulfur spit.

At close quarters, its Snap Bite strikes in 4 ticks dealing 7.0 damage and setting prey ablaze. Beyond reach or when enemies attempt to pillar upward, it expels a Brimstone Spit that erupts into a lingering 2x2 Burning Tar Pool, trapping victims in Slowness II.

A raised shield will absorb the Snap Bite and stun the salamander for an extra 10 ticks. Backing up beyond 2.6 blocks causes it to cancel its strike into a short cooldown. When surrounded by two or more foes, it unleashes a sweeping Tail Whip to cast flankers away.
I: Brimstone Scale. II: Magma Cream & Coal.
Yields Magma Cream and Coal upon defeat, with a 35% chance to drop a prized Brimstone Scale—an unyielding volcanic scute used for thermal protection infusions and hardened fey equipment.
advancements.codenamecoraline.bosses.fin: Encounter a living Brimstone Salamander along the lava shores of the Nether.
advancements.codenamecoraline.bosses.bri: Obtain an intact Brimstone Scale from the fiery amphibian.
entity.codenamecoraline.architect.summon: A statue rises. It holds the Commandments... and waits.
The tablet must rest on top of a solid block.
No god answers in a peaceful world.
There is no room for the statue here (it needs 2 x 4 free blocks).
Another Architect already watches over this place.
The tablet is inert and cold.
item.codenamecoraline.architect_scimitar: Right-click raises the blade: a blow or projectile from the front at the right moment is parried.
After a parry, your next hit within 2 s deals +60% damage (Reprise).
advancements.codenamecoraline.bosses.arc: Chiseled deepslate, amethyst and a diamond: the tablet a stone god once carried. Obtain the Commandment Tablet.
Set the tablet on a solid block. The statue that rises waits for someone to wake it.
Defeat Kandiaru, the Architect, Administrator of the Temple.
Of the six scimitars, only the dominant one survived the fall. Pick up the Architect's Scimitar.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.architect.name: The Architect
bestiary.codenamecoraline.architect.anat: Six arms, six scimitars and stone wings.

A 4.7-block statue of blue-grey stone, hooded, in a long stone coat, with a two-piece mask, gargoyle wings of carved plates and six arms holding six basalt scimitars. His eyes are black with coral irises; a diamond seal glows on his chest and brow.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.architect.stat: He starts as a statue holding the Commandment Tablet and only wakes when a player strikes him. The waking lasts 5.5 s: the mask falls in two halves, the tablet breaks on the ground and he laughs. Nobody near him takes damage meanwhile. To raise him, use the tablet on a solid block, outside peaceful, with 2 x 4 blocks of room and no other Architect within 96 blocks.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.architect.temp: They say the temple had a god and the god had an administrator. Kandiaru measured every stone and every worshipper and wrote the commandments on his own tablet. When the temple fell he became a statue at his post, waiting for someone to break the order.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.architect.blad: The Sixfold Edict, cut by cut.

Sixfold Edict (six cuts in a row), Crossed Mandate (a high and a low X), Cartenon Wheel (a spin at three heights), Splitter Crescent (a low sweep and a vertical chop), Piercing Sentence (a long thrust), Verdict Hammer (a heavy blow that disables a shield), False Verdict (a feint, a pause and a late chop) and Rushing Rebuke (a charge and two cuts) and, in the second phase, the Gargoyle Fall: he leaps and lands on runes marked on the ground.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.architect.edic: Every blow has a visible wind-up and its direction locks when it starts: step to the side. If you leave his reach he cancels the blow instead of cutting the air. At 70% health he takes command (phase 2); at 35% he laughs and enters the Collapse, more aggressive and chaining blows. He follows no one beyond 36 blocks from where he woke, and whoever climbs a pillar gets the Gargoyle Fall. He never stands still: he circles, backs away, sidesteps and hops back, reads who is ready to strike and counters right after. Whoever lives behind a shield gets the Hammer, which lowers it for 5 s; dodge it and use the long recovery.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.architect.parr: He parries blows from the front and answers with a quick Reprise, at most twice in a row. His guard halves frontal damage, and common arrows, snowballs and eggs are deflected. Heavy blows fill his posture; a full posture stuns him for 1.5 s with the chest exposed, after which he cannot be stunned again for 10 s. Strike from behind and during the recovery of his spins.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.architect.spoi: What Is Left of the Temple
I: Scimitar. II: Tablet. III: Face.

On defeat: 500 XP and the Architect's Scimitar, always. The Commandment Tablet is crafted from chiseled deepslate, amethyst shards and a diamond. The advancements Commandments in Stone, A Statue That Watches, Administration Revoked and The First Blade keep the story.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.architect.scim: 9 damage, speed 1.8. Right-click raises the blade for 0.8 s; between 0.1 and 0.5 s, a blow or projectile from the front is parried: the attacker is slowed and weakened for 2 s and light projectiles fly back. The parry charges the Reprise: your next hit within 2 s deals +60%. A landed parry recharges in 3 s, a missed one in 5 s. Explosions, fire and magic cannot be parried. Against the Architect, each parry weighs on his posture.
